summary: Source decomposition from six primary sources read directly: Jetchev-Skinner-Wan (Sections 1.1-1.3 in full, 3.3, 6.1-6.2, 7.2-7.3.1), Bump-Friedberg-Hoffstein Sec. 0 (read from 150 dpi page images, since the scan has no text layer), Castella's ERRATUM in full, Castella-Grossi-Skinner Sec. 1, Keller-Yin Sections 0.1-0.3 and 4.2, and Wei Zhang's survey Sections 1.4-1.5. The decomposition follows the stage texts' insistence on named branches with their exact hypotheses. Four points are worth flagging. (1) BFH's theorem produces ONE fundamental discriminant for each finite set S of primes containing those dividing the level; it is not a density statement and does not directly give the infinitely many twists the stage wants, and the iteration producing infinitely many is recorded here as AUTHORED. (2) JSW's rank-one theorem needs TWO different auxiliary imaginary quadratic fields and a Shimura-curve parameterization with N^- > 1 (explicitly NOT the classical Heegner setting), and its p = 3 supersingular proviso is consumed at exactly one place: the final invocation of the rank-zero formula for the second twist. (3) Castella's original Theorem A is WITHDRAWN when p exactly divides N: the erratum identifies the defect (a point of the Hida family used in [Cas18, Thm. 4.2] need not exist) and replaces it by Theorem A', which ADDS the nonsplit-multiplicative condition on q and E(Q_p)[p] = 0 while DROPPING semistability. (4) Keller-Yin's broader Eisenstein branch keeps the torsion denominator (#E(Q)_tors)^2 explicitly and needs a torsion-tolerant anticyclotomic control theorem (their Appendix B), because their imprimitive Selmer groups can have finite Lambda-submodules so characteristic ideals are no longer Fitting ideals; their multiplicative-reduction theorem is a main conjecture only, conditional on extending CGS to higher weight. Every source read excludes p = 2 and additive primes, so no BSD.8 certificate can be assembled from them. Stages BSD.1, BSD.8 and BSD.9 are marked not_read; the other nine are partial. BSTW 2024 and CGLS 2022, both named as normative by the stage texts and both PRESENT in the library, were not opened by this job and are recorded as unread-but-available boundaries. [Corrected in review REVIEW-EXT-08-EXT-16. (a) Point (2) overstates JSW. The 'N^- > 1' sentence comes from the introduction (p. 3), but the proof takes N^- = 1 and N^+ = q, with q ramified in K', when N = q is prime (Sec. 7.4.1, p. 45). For K'' it takes N^- = N/q_1, which is 1 when N is prime (Sec. 7.4.2, p. 47). What Theorems 6.1.4-6.1.6 actually need is (gen-H) plus one prime divisor of N that is non-split in K. JSW choose K' and K'' by Friedberg-Hoffstein [FH95, Thm. B], which allows inert and ramified conditions; BFH 1990 prescribes only splitting. (b) The supersingular case of JSW Theorem 1.2.1 rests on [Wan14a] (inside Theorem 6.1.4) and [Wan14b] (Theorem 7.2.1(iii)). Both arXiv preprints were checked on 2026-09-16 and are WITHDRAWN. arXiv:1411.6352 is 'superseded by part of' BSTW arXiv:2409.01350. arXiv:1412.1767 was rewritten as Castella-Liu-Wan arXiv:2109.08375. (c) Point (4) gives the wrong cause. Keller-Yin's remark that characteristic ideals are no longer Fitting ideals, so one passes to free parts (Sec. 0.2, p. 5), concerns the Hida-family proof of the multiplicative-reduction Theorem D (Sec. 5.1). The Appendix B control theorem is needed because their lattice and residual set-up allows nontrivial torsion (Sec. 0.5, p. 6; Sec. 4.2, p. 42). (d) Locators were fixed. CGS Theorem A and Greenberg's mu-bound are on p. 2. Keller-Yin's Theorems C and D and the remark after D are on p. 5. Zhang's Theorem 1.5 is in Sec. 1.4 on p. 7. (e) papers/ADD_RT97.pdf is Rohrlich-Tunnell, not Ribet-Takahashi, and papers/R02_KI_WanNonordinary.pdf is not JSW's [Wan14a]. (f) Open question: Keller-Yin's Sec. 4.2 text does not show the rank-zero input when phi|G_p is 1 or omega (see gaps). All six library hashes match.]

nodes.title: The quadratic-twist completed L-function, its functional equation, and the sign rule under a splitting condition
nodes.statement: For f a normalized newform on Gamma_0(M) of even weight k with trivial character, set Lambda(s,f) = (2 pi)^{-s} Gamma(s) M^{s/2} L(s,f); it satisfies Lambda(s,f) = epsilon Lambda(k-s,f) with epsilon = +-1. For D a fundamental discriminant let chi_D be the Kronecker character of conductor |D|, so chi_D(-1) = sgn(D). Put L(s,f,chi_D) = sum chi_D(n) a(n) n^{-s} and Lambda(s,f,chi_D) = (D^2 M)^{s/2}(2 pi)^{-s} Gamma(s) L(s,f,chi_D). This continues analytically and, PROVIDED gcd(M,D) = 1, satisfies Lambda(s,f,chi_D) = epsilon chi_D(-M) Lambda(k-s,f,chi_D). If moreover every prime dividing M splits in Q(sqrt(D)), then chi_D(M) = 1 and the sign of the twisted functional equation equals epsilon if D > 0 and is opposite to epsilon if D < 0. Also, ord_{s=k/2} L(s,f) is even when epsilon = +1 and odd when epsilon = -1. [Annotated in review: BFH state this parity immediately after the UNTWISTED functional equation ('Clearly the order of vanishing ...', printed p. 543). It does not follow from the twisted sign rule, as the earlier word 'Consequently' suggested.]
hypotheses: f is a CUSPIDAL NEWFORM of EVEN weight k with TRIVIAL character on Gamma_0(M)

gcd(M,D) = 1 is required for the displayed twisted functional equation; without it the twisted form need not be a newform of the stated level [Annotated in review: only the first clause is BFH's ('provided gcd(M,D) = 1', printed p. 543). The explanation after the semicolon is authored.]
The splitting condition 'every prime dividing M splits in Q(sqrt D)' is what converts chi_D(M) = 1 into the sign rule; it is the Heegner-type hypothesis
chi_D(-1) = sgn(D) is the input that makes the D > 0 and D < 0 cases differ
[Added in review: if every prime dividing M splits in Q(sqrt D), then no prime dividing M ramifies, so gcd(M,D) = 1 holds automatically in the splitting case.]
proofSteps: Record the completed L-function and its functional equation with the sign epsilon.
Record the twisted completed L-function and its functional equation under gcd(M,D) = 1.
Evaluate chi_D(-M) = chi_D(-1)chi_D(M) = sgn(D) under the splitting hypothesis chi_D(M) = 1.
Read off the parity of the order of vanishing at the centre s = k/2.
acceptance: Instantiate at k = 2 and f attached to an elliptic curve E of conductor N and check the factorization L(E/K,s) = L(E,s)L(E^D,s)
Check the sign rule on a curve with epsilon = -1 and a positive fundamental discriminant
Check that dropping gcd(M,D) = 1 breaks the displayed functional equation

nodes.title: Existence of quadratic twists with prescribed splitting and either a simple zero or a nonzero central value
nodes.statement: Let f be a cuspidal newform of even weight k with trivial character for Gamma_0(M), let S be a FINITE SET OF PRIMES INCLUDING ALL THOSE DIVIDING M, and let epsilon be the sign in the functional equation of f. Then (i) there exists a fundamental discriminant D with epsilon D < 0 such that every prime in S splits in Q(sqrt D) and L(s,f,chi_D) has a SIMPLE ZERO at s = k/2; and (ii) there exists a fundamental discriminant D with epsilon D > 0 such that every prime in S splits in Q(sqrt D) and L(k/2,f,chi_D) is NONZERO.
hypotheses: f is a cuspidal newform of EVEN weight k with TRIVIAL character on Gamma_0(M); the theorem is not stated for nontrivial nebentypus
S is any finite set of primes CONTAINING those dividing M; the conclusion produces a D for that S, so prescribing more splitting conditions is allowed by enlarging S

The theorem produces ONE fundamental discriminant for each S, not a density statement and not an a priori infinite family. Obtaining infinitely many D requires iterating with enlarged S; that iteration is AUTHORED here, not quoted. [Checked in review, REVIEWER COMPUTATION (not a source statement): the iteration works. Q(sqrt D_1) is a quadratic field, so D_1 != 1 and some prime l divides D_1. Adding every such l to S forces l to split in Q(sqrt D_2), while l ramifies in Q(sqrt D_1), so D_2 != D_1. Repeating with all earlier discriminants added gives infinitely many distinct D.]
Both conclusions are about the CENTRAL point s = k/2 of the analytic normalization
The proof reduces to epsilon = +1 by twisting f by an odd quadratic character whose ramification lies outside S; this reduction is itself part of the theorem's proof, and it changes the form

[Added in review: SCOPE LIMIT. BFH prescribe only SPLITTING of the primes in S. They cannot impose inert or ramified local conditions. Several consumers in this packet need exactly such conditions: JSW's K' (q inert or ramified) and K'' (every prime of N^- inert), both chosen by Friedberg-Hoffstein [FH95, Thm. B] (JSW Sec. 7.4.1, p. 45 and Sec. 7.4.2, p. 47); CGS's worked examples with psi(5) = -1 (CGS p. 5, [FH95, Thm. B.1/B.2]); and Castella's Theorem 1.1, which needs at least one nonsplit q || N. None of these selections is supplied by this node.]

[Added in review: BFH record on printed p. 544 that 'the second assertion was proved by a different technique by Waldspurger [19] and [20]. See also Kohnen [12] and Jacquet [10].' Part (ii) therefore has earlier, independent proofs.]
proofSteps: Reduce to epsilon = +1 by twisting outside S (BFH state this explicitly).

Form a Dirichlet series in an auxiliary parameter u whose D-th coefficient is L(s,f,chi_D), via an integral transform applied to a half-integral weight Eisenstein series on the metaplectic double cover of GSp(4,R); there are two such series, for positive and negative discriminants.

Study the poles in u of these Dirichlet series. Two poles, corresponding to two cells of the Bruhat decomposition on GSp(4), coalesce when s = k/2; one contribution is explicitly computed and the other carries a Dirichlet series with an Euler product whose ramified factors at primes of S are not computed explicitly.

Use Jacobi modular forms (automorphic forms on the semidirect product of GSp(4,R) with a Heisenberg group) so that the theta multiplier is built into the framework and the sifting of the chi_D with prescribed splitting is achieved.
Note the boundary: the details of the residue/positivity argument were NOT read in this pass; only the introduction was read.
acceptance: Check the sign bookkeeping: for epsilon = +1 part (i) produces D < 0, which is the imaginary quadratic field needed for a Heegner point
Check that S can be enlarged to force any finite list of splitting conditions
Check the consequence BFH themselves record: (i) combined with Kolyvagin and Gross-Zagier gives finiteness of E(Q) and of Sha for a modular E with L(1,E) nonzero
Construct the iteration producing infinitely many D and verify it

sources.excerpt: Theorem. Let f be cuspidal newform of even weight k with trivial character for the group Gamma_0(M), and let S be a finite set of primes including all those dividing M. Let epsilon denote the sign in the functional equation of f. (i) There exists a quadratic field Q(sqrt D) with D a fundamental discriminant, and epsilon D < 0, such that every prime in S splits in Q(sqrt D), and L(s,f,chi_D) has a simple zero at s = k/2. (ii) There exists a quadratic field Q(sqrt D) with D a fundamental discriminant, and epsilon D > 0, such that every prime in S splits in Q(sqrt D), and L(k/2,f,chi_D) is nonzero.

nodes.title: Analytic rank at most one implies equality of ranks and finiteness of Sha
nodes.statement: For E/Q an elliptic curve, if r_an(E/Q) <= 1 then r_an(E/Q) = r_MW(E/Q) and Sha(E/Q) is finite. The proof combines the Gross-Zagier formula with Kolyvagin's Heegner-point Euler system, and requires a suitable auxiliary imaginary quadratic field whose existence comes from the analytic nonvanishing theorem of BSD.2.
hypotheses: The theorem is for elliptic curves over Q; S. Zhang generalized it to many modular elliptic curves and GL_2-type modular abelian varieties over totally real fields
The auxiliary imaginary quadratic field is NOT optional: Zhang's survey states explicitly that the proof requires it and that its existence is an analytic-number-theory input
Modularity of E is presupposed (the Heegner points come from a modular parameterization)
For r_an = 0 there is an INDEPENDENT proof by Kato via his Euler system, and one by Bertolini-Darmon for the rank statement; for CM curves Coates-Wiles proved the rank-zero statement earlier
proofSteps: Choose an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field K by the nonvanishing theorem of BSD.2, with the splitting (Heegner) condition at the primes dividing the conductor and with the correct sign branch.
Apply the Gross-Zagier formula to relate the Neron-Tate height of a Heegner point in E(K) to the central derivative of L(E/K,s).
Apply Kolyvagin's Euler-system argument to bound the Selmer group, obtaining rank one and finiteness of Sha over K.
Descend to Q using the factorization L(E/K,s) = L(E,s)L(E^D,s) and the rank identity.

NOTE: neither Gross-Zagier's paper nor Gross's exposition of Kolyvagin's work has a text layer in the supplied library, so the internal structure of these two steps was NOT read; only the packaged statement in Zhang's survey and in JSW's introduction was read.
acceptance: Check the two sign branches: for r_an(E) = 1 use BFH (ii) to make L(E^D,1) nonzero, and for r_an(E) = 0 use BFH (i) to make L(E^D,s) have a simple zero
Check that the resulting K satisfies the Heegner condition at every prime dividing N
Check the descent of finiteness of Sha along the quadratic extension

Bertolini and Darmon in [4] also prove that if r_an(E/Q) = 0, then r_MW(E/Q) = 0. nodes.title: Rationality of L'(E,1)/(Reg . Omega) and the comparison of Tamagawa numbers and periods under quadratic base change
nodes.statement: It is a consequence of the Gross-Zagier formula that L'(E/Q,1)/(Reg(E/Q) . Omega_E) lies in Q^x, so its p-adic valuation is defined; the same holds for L(E/Q,1)/Omega_E in analytic rank zero. For an imaginary quadratic field K of discriminant -D and E^D the quadratic twist, the Tamagawa numbers over K and over Q are related by ord_p(product over w of c_w(E/K)) = ord_p(product over l of c_l(E/Q) . product over l of c_l(E^D/Q)), and there is a corresponding comparison of periods; both are used to convert a bound over K into a bound over Q. [Corrected in review: JSW's (7.3.a) is stated for K = Q(sqrt D) of discriminant D < 0 (Sec. 7.3.1, p. 43), although the opening of Sec. 7.3 writes K = Q(sqrt -D). JSW add: 'Here we have also used that E has good reduction at p and so has Tamagawa number 1 at any place dividing p.' Good reduction at p is therefore part of the comparison as used. The period comparison is (7.3.e), Omega_f^cong = sqrt|D| . Omega_E . Omega_{E^D} up to a p-adic unit (Sec. 7.3.2, p. 44). It is derived from three relations: (7.3.b) ([Ski14b, Sec. 3.3], [GV00, Prop. 3.1]); (7.3.c) ([SZ14, Lem. 9.5]); and (7.3.d) ([SZ14, Lem. 9.6], for rho-bar_{E,p} irreducible, p not dividing D and p split in K). It enters the proof in (7.4.c) on p. 46.]

nodes.title: The Jetchev-Skinner-Wan p-part formula for semistable curves of analytic rank one
nodes.statement: Let E/Q be a SEMISTABLE elliptic curve of conductor N (so N is squarefree) with ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = 1, and let p be a prime of GOOD reduction (p not dividing N) with rho_{E,p} irreducible. If p >= 5, then ord_p(L'(E,1)/(Reg(E/Q) . Omega_E)) = ord_p(#Sha(E/Q) . product over finite l of c_l(E/Q)). If p = 3, the same holds PROVIDED a_p(E) = 0 when E has supersingular reduction at p.
hypotheses: E must be SEMISTABLE (N squarefree). This is separate from the hypothesis that p is a prime of GOOD reduction; the stage's warning not to conflate the two is exactly right
p is a prime of good reduction with E[p] irreducible; p >= 5, or p = 3 with a_p(E) = 0 in the supersingular case

The formula as displayed omits the torsion denominator (#E(Q)_tor)^2 present in Conjecture 1.1.1; that is legitimate here only because p >= 3 and E[p] irreducible force p not to divide #E(Q)_tor. The general BSD statement retains the torsion factor

CM curves are excluded from the hypotheses (a CM E is not semistable), but JSW note the conclusion follows for them from Kobayashi's p-adic Gross-Zagier formula together with the main conjectures [Corrected in review: JSW's sentence (p. 2) also requires the non-vanishing of the p-adic height of the Heegner point, and cites [Kob13, Cor. 1.4]. [Kob13] is 'The p-adic Gross-Zagier formula for elliptic curves at supersingular primes'.]

The proof needs TWO different auxiliary imaginary quadratic fields: K' for the lower bound and K'' for the upper bound. [Corrected in review. The earlier text also required 'a Shimura-curve parameterization X_{N^+,N^-} with N^- > 1 (so NOT the classical Heegner-point setting)', quoting the introduction (p. 3). The proof is more precise. For K' (Sec. 7.4.1, p. 45) JSW require (a) (gen-H), (b) q = q_1 inert or ramified in K', (c) p split and (d) L(E^{D'},1) != 0. If N has at least two prime factors, q may be taken inert, which forces N^- > 1. If N = q is prime, JSW take N^- = 1 and N^+ = q with q ramified in K', where only (gen-H) holds. For K'' (Sec. 7.4.2, p. 47): if N has r prime factors with r odd, N^+ = q_1 and N^- = N/q_1; if r is even, N^+ = 1 and N^- = N. So N^- = 1, the classical Heegner setting on X_0(N), when N is prime. Theorems 6.1.4-6.1.6 and Prop. 6.2.1 need (gen-H) together with at least one prime divisor of N non-split in K. Both fields are chosen by Friedberg-Hoffstein [FH95, Thm. B], not by the BFH theorem of BSD.2.]

[Added in review: PROVENANCE OF THE SUPERSINGULAR CASE. Theorem 6.1.4 cites [Wan13, Thm. 1.1] and [Wan14a, Thm. 1.1] under (good) = 'p does not divide N' (p. 22), which includes supersingular p. The final step uses 'the proved cases of the cyclotomic main conjectures for E^{D''} (see [SU13, Thm.2(a)] and [Ski14b, Thm.C] for the ordinary case and [Wan14b, Thm.1.3] for the supersingular case)' (p. 4), via Theorem 7.2.1(iii) = [Wan14b, Cor. 4.8] (p. 42). JSW's bibliography identifies [Wan14a] as 'Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin-Selberg p-adic L-functions: non-ordinary case' and [Wan14b] as 'Iwasawa main conjecture for supersingular elliptic curves'. The arXiv records of both were checked on 2026-09-16 and both are WITHDRAWN. arXiv:1412.1767 'is completely re-written ... as arXiv:2109.08375' (Castella-Liu-Wan, library papers/BSD_CLW.pdf). arXiv:1411.6352 'is superseded by part of the new preprint 2409.01350' (BSTW; Remark 1.4(i)). As sourced in this packet, the supersingular case of Theorem 1.2.1 therefore rests on withdrawn preprints. This node has not checked that CLW and BSTW prove exactly the statements JSW use; BSTW's twist range is narrower than JSW 7.2.1(iii) (see the rank-zero node). JSW Sec. 7.4.4(iii) (p. 48) confirms that the p = 3 proviso a_p = 0 is 'only because the same hypothesis is made in [Wan14b]'.]
proofSteps: LOWER BOUND. Choose K' and prove the anticyclotomic control theorem (Theorem 3.3.1) comparing a Lambda-cotorsion Selmer group with a Z_p-cotorsion one, with an explicit constant C^Sigma(W) built from local H^0, H^1_ur and H^1 terms at split primes. [Corrected in review: in Theorem 3.3.1 (p. 14) the two H^0 factors are at the places v and vbar above p. The H^1_ur factors run over the SPLIT w in S_p minus Sigma, and the H^1 factors over ALL w in Sigma. JSW's S_p is the set of places of S NOT dividing p (p. 13). Prop. 6.2.1 additionally assumes (corank 1) and (sur); for K' these follow from rank E(K') = 1 and the finiteness of Sha(E/K') (p. 45).]

[Corrected in review.] Wan's Theorem 6.1.4 is a TWO-VARIABLE divisibility: char(X^Sigma_Gr(M)) Lambda_{K,R}[1/p] is contained in (L^Sigma_p(f)) for Hida's two-variable p-adic L-function. It assumes (irredK), (split), (gen-H), (good) and (-free), at least one prime divisor of N non-split in K, and Sigma containing all places dividing N D_K (p. 39). Combined with Corollaries 3.4.2 and 5.3.2, it gives Theorem 6.1.5 (p. 40): the ANTICYCLOTOMIC divisibility char(X^Sigma_ac(M)) Lambda_R[1/p] in (L^Sigma_p(f)), for the BDP/Brooks/LZZ p-adic L-function, under the same hypotheses. Theorem 6.1.6 (p. 40) upgrades this to Lambda_R and DROPS the condition that Sigma contain the places dividing N D_K. Its proof compares Sigma_1 and Sigma_2 through the Euler factors P_w using the surjectivity of (3.3.a) (Proposition 3.3.3), and removes the p-ambiguity for Sigma empty using Burungale's mu = 0 result (Proposition 5.1.3). The earlier text attributed the anticyclotomic Lambda_R[1/p] divisibility to Theorem 6.1.4.

Combine with Brooks's central value formula (a BDP-type formula outside the range of interpolation, expressing the p-adic L-value as the p-adic logarithm of a Heegner point) to get inequality (1.3.a), which involves the index [E(K') : Z z_{K'}]^2 and the Tamagawa numbers at the SPLIT primes.

Convert (1.3.a) into an L-value statement using the general Gross-Zagier formula of Zhang and of Yuan-Zhang-Zhang for the Shimura-curve point, where the Ribet-Takahashi degree ratio produces the Tamagawa numbers at the non-split primes. [Annotated in review: that is the outline (p. 3). The proof (Sec. 7.4.1, p. 46) uses 'the variant of the Gross-Zagier formula for the Heegner point z_{K'} [Zha14, p. 245]', which footnote 9 calls a special case of a formula in [CST14]. There delta(N,1)/delta(N^+,N^-) equals the product of c_l(E/K') over l | N^- up to a p-adic unit, which gives (7.4.c). JSW's [Zha14] is W. Zhang, 'Selmer groups and the indivisibility of Heegner points' (library papers/BSD_ZhangIndivisibility.pdf). [CST14] is Cai-Shu-Tian (library papers/BSD_YZZExplicit.pdf). Neither was opened.]

Descend from K' to Q using the Tamagawa/period dictionary and Kato's proved upper bound for the twist E^{D'} (chosen so that L(E^{D'},1) is nonzero). [Annotated in review: on p. 47 JSW combine (7.4.b), (7.4.c) and (7.3.a) for K = K' with Sha(E/K')[p^infinity] = Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity] + Sha(E^{D'}/Q)[p^infinity] and Theorem 7.2.1(i) for E^{D'}, which gives (7.4.d).]

UPPER BOUND. Choose a different field K'' with each prime dividing N^+ split and each prime dividing N^- inert, and a Shimura-curve parameterization for which no Tamagawa number at a prime dividing N^+ is divisible by p; run Kolyvagin's Euler system argument to get (1.3.b), then use the Gross-Zagier formula again and the known lower bound for the twist E^{D''} (from the cyclotomic main conjectures of Skinner-Urban, Skinner and Wan). [Annotated in review: K'' must also have p split and L(E^{D''},1) != 0; the latter comes from Friedberg-Hoffstein (p. 47). The Kolyvagin bound is Theorem 4.4.1. The descent uses (7.3.a) for K = K'' and Theorem 7.2.1(ii) or (iii) for E^{D''}, giving (7.4.e) on p. 48. In the supersingular case the Wan input is a withdrawn preprint; see the provenance hypothesis.]
The hypothesis a_p(E) = 0 for p = 3 supersingular is needed ONLY at the final step, where the p-part of the BSD formula for L(E^{D''},1) is invoked.
acceptance: Check Remark 7.2.2: the condition a_p(E) = 0 in Theorem 7.2.1(iii) is superfluous for p >= 5

Check where square-free N is used: JSW Sec. 7.4.4(i)-(ii) (p. 48) say it is assumed in [Bro14] (Proposition 5.1.6) and in [Wan13], [Wan14b], and could be replaced by 'principal series or Steinberg at each l | N'; (gen-H) itself only needs N^- square-free. [Corrected in review: the earlier item tied semistability to a factorization with N^- > 1, which the proof does not always use.]
Check that p >= 3 with E[p] irreducible forces p not to divide #E(Q)_tor, so that the torsion factor may be omitted

Compare with Zhang's Theorem 1.6 and with Berti-Bertolini-Venerucci Theorem A and confirm JSW's statement that those carry extra hypotheses (respectively a ramification condition at l congruent to +-1 mod p, and p non-anomalous with p not dividing any c_l)

nodes.title: The rank-zero p-part results of JSW Theorem 7.2.1, in three separate branches
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good or multiplicative reduction at the ODD prime p, with rho_{E,p} irreducible, and suppose L(E,1) is nonzero. (i) ord_p(#Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity]) <= ord_p(L(E/Q,1)/(Omega_E product_l c_l(E))). (ii) IF E has good ORDINARY or MULTIPLICATIVE reduction at p AND there exists a prime q of MULTIPLICATIVE reduction for E at which rho_{E,p} is RAMIFIED, then equality holds. (iii) IF E is semistable, or a quadratic twist of a semistable curve by a character unramified at the primes dividing the conductor of the semistable curve, and E has SUPERSINGULAR reduction at p with a_p(E) = 0, then equality holds.
hypotheses: p is ODD; the three parts have different reduction hypotheses and must not be merged
Part (ii)'s auxiliary prime q must be a prime of MULTIPLICATIVE reduction at which the residual representation is RAMIFIED. This is the Skinner-Urban/Skinner hypothesis

Part (iii) permits a quadratic twist of a semistable curve, but only by a character unramified at the primes dividing the conductor of the semistable curve; JSW note (Remark 7.2.3) that this is slightly more general than the cited [Wan14b] statement and explain why the semistability was imposed there (to avoid local triple product integrals for supercuspidal representations at split primes)
Part (iii)'s condition a_p(E) = 0 is superfluous for p >= 5 (Remark 7.2.2)
Part (i) is only an INEQUALITY and holds under the weakest hypotheses; it is Kato's bound

[Added in review: PROVENANCE. JSW attribute (i) to Kato via [PR03, Thm. 4.8], (ii) to [SU13, Thm. 2] and [Ski14b, Thm. C], and (iii) to [Wan14b, Cor. 4.8] (p. 42). [Wan14b] is arXiv:1411.6352, WITHDRAWN and 'superseded by part of' BSTW arXiv:2409.01350 (checked 2026-09-16). No current source in this packet supports part (iii). BSTW's replacement statements have a NARROWER twist range. Theorem 1.3 (p. 3) and Theorem 1.5 (p. 4) assume E semistable and p > 2 supersingular, with (1.7) if p = 3, and extend only to twists E^K 'with discriminant coprime to Np and divisible only by primes of ordinary reduction for E'. JSW's (iii) allows any quadratic twist of a semistable curve by a character unramified at the primes dividing its conductor. The stage forbids silently broadening the twist range.]
proofSteps: Record the three branches verbatim with their hypotheses.
Record Remarks 7.2.2 and 7.2.3, which delimit the a_p = 0 condition and the twist generality.
Record that (i) is used in the rank-one proof for the twist E^{D'} and that (ii)/(iii) are used for E^{D''}.
acceptance: Check that an E with good ordinary reduction at p but no ramified multiplicative prime q falls under (i) only
Check the supersingular branch on a semistable curve with a_p = 0

Compare with Zhang's Theorem 1.5 (Kato, Skinner-Urban), which requires p >= 3, good ordinary reduction, rho_{E,p} SURJECTIVE and a prime l exactly dividing N with rho_{E,p} ramified; JSW's (ii) requires only irreducibility and allows multiplicative reduction at p. Sigma 3 (2015)), which is not withdrawn.]

(2) rho_{E,p} is surjective. (3) There exists a prime l exactly dividing N such that rho_{E,p} is ramified at l. If L(E,1) is nonzero, then the p-part of the B-SD formula holds ... Remark 8. nodes.title: Castella's corrected anticyclotomic main conjecture and Theorem A' at multiplicative primes
nodes.statement: THEOREM 1.1 (corrected). Let E/Q be an elliptic curve of conductor N with multiplicative reduction at p > 3, and let K be an imaginary quadratic field such that there exists an ideal N of O_K with O_K/N isomorphic to Z/NZ and in which p = p pbar SPLITS. Assume (i) E[p] is irreducible as a G_Q-module; (ii) if 2 is nonsplit in K then 2 exactly divides N; (iii) E has NONSPLIT multiplicative reduction at each prime q exactly dividing N which is nonsplit in K, and there is at least one such q at which E[p] is ramified; (iv) E(Q_p)[p] = 0. Then Ch_Lambda(X_ac(E[p^infinity])) is Lambda-torsion and Ch_Lambda(X_ac(E[p^infinity])) Lambda_{R_0} = (L_p(f)). THEOREM A'. Let E/Q have multiplicative reduction at p > 3, E[p] irreducible, nonsplit multiplicative reduction at some prime q not equal to p where E[p] is ramified, and E(Q_p)[p] = 0. If ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = 1 then ord_p(L'(E,1)/(Reg(E/Q) Omega_E)) = ord_p(#Sha(E/Q) product_{l | N} c_l(E/Q)).
hypotheses: p > 3 and E has MULTIPLICATIVE reduction at p

THE ORIGINAL THEOREM A OF [Cas18] IS WITHDRAWN IN THE CASE p EXACTLY DIVIDING N: the erratum states that the existence of a point phi in X_I^a used in the proof of [Cas18, Thm. 4.2] 'is not guaranteed in general', which invalidates the proof of [Cas18, Thm. 4.4] [Annotated in review: the erratum's words are that this 'affects the proof of [op. cit., Thm. 4.4]' and that Theorem A' 'should replace the main Theorem A in op. cit. when p || N' (p. 1). 'Withdrawn' and 'invalidates' are paraphrases; the erratum does not assert that the original statement is false.]

Compared with the original Theorem A, Theorem A' ADDS two hypotheses (the auxiliary prime q must be of NONSPLIT multiplicative reduction, and E(Q_p)[p] = 0) and REMOVES the semistability requirement, so additive primes elsewhere are permitted

Hypothesis (ii) originates in [Wan20, CLW22] where it handles a technicality at 2; hypothesis (iii) mostly arises from [Hsi14]; Castella states that both 'should have been included in [Cas18, Thm. 4.4]' and are inherited from the final versions of the quoted results
Hypothesis (iv) is NEW and is forced by the need for the imprimitive Selmer groups Sel^Sigma_p(K_infinity, A_f) to behave well under congruences

Castella notes that by Tate's p-adic uniformization, (iv) is equivalent to condition (b) of [SZ14, Thm. 1.1] when E has split multiplicative reduction at p, i.e. p does not divide ord_p(q_E) and log_p(q_E) lies in p Z_p^x

[Added in review, REVIEWER COMPUTATION (not a source statement): K must have an ideal N with O_K/N = Z/NZ. An inert prime has no ideal of norm q, and for a ramified q the only ideal of norm q^2 is (q), with non-cyclic quotient. So every 'nonsplit' q || N in (iii) is RAMIFIED in K, and any q with q^2 | N must split. Theorem 1.1 thus needs at least one ramified prime q, which the splitting-only BFH theorem cannot supply.]
proofSteps: Lemma 2.1: for Sigma containing all primes v not dividing p where T_g is ramified, with rho-bar_g restricted to G_K irreducible and H^0(K_p, A_g[uniformizer]) = 0, the inclusion M_g[uniformizer^m] into M_g induces an isomorphism Sel^Sigma_p(K, M_g[uniformizer^m]) = Sel^Sigma_p(K, M_g)[uniformizer^m]. The proof uses Shapiro's lemma and the vanishing of H^0(K,M_g), and the hypothesis H^0(K_p, A_g[uniformizer]) = 0 is exactly what kills the kernel of H^1(K_p, M_g[uniformizer^m]) -> H^1(K_p,M_g)[uniformizer^m].
Lemma 2.2: if X_ac(A_g) is Lambda_O-torsion then Sel^Sigma_p(K,M_g) has no proper finite index Lambda_O-submodules; quoted as a special case of Greenberg [Gre16].

The remainder of the erratum's Sec. 2 (the congruence argument avoiding [Cas18, Thm. 4.2]) was NOT read in this pass. [Updated in review: the reviewer read it (pp. 3-4). Theorem 2.3, for p-ordinary g of weight k >= 2 and level M >= 3 with p not dividing M under (i)-(iv), extends [Cas18, Thm. 4.1] to higher weight. It is proved from [CH18, (4.7), Sec. 5.2, Thms. 5.7 and 6.1], [LV19, Thm. 4.7], [CGS23, Thm. 5.5.1], [CGLS22, Sec. 3.3.1, Rems. 3.3.5 and 4.1.3], [Cha05, Thm. 2], [BCK21, Thm. 5.2], [FW21, Thm. 4.41] with [EW16] and the mu = 0 theorem [Hsi14, Thm. B], [FO12, Cor. 7.2.1], [CGS23, Prop. 1.4.5], [JSW17, Cor. 3.4.2] and the argument of [JSW17, Thm. 6.1.6]. Theorem 1.1 is then proved on p. 4 following [Ski16, Sec. 3.1]. That proof uses Hida-family congruent forms g_m ([Ski16, Sec. 2.6], [Cas20, Thm. 2.11]), Theorem 2.3, Lemma 2.2 (so that Ch = Fitt), Lemma 2.1, [Ski16, p. 192], the nonvanishing of L_p(f) from Cornut-Vatsal [CV07] with [Cas20, Thm. 5.3], [Ski20, Lem. 2.8.1] and [FO12, Lem. 2.14]. Hypothesis (iv), E(Q_p)[p] = 0, enters through Lemma 2.1's condition H^0(K_p, A[varpi]) = 0 (K_p = Q_p). None of the imports was read.]
Theorem A' then follows by the same argument as [Cas18, Sec. 5] with Theorem 1.1 in place of [Cas18, Thm. 4.4].

nodes.statement: THEOREM C (= Theorem 4.2.1). Let E/Q be an elliptic curve and p > 2 a prime of GOOD reduction. Assume E admits a cyclic p-isogeny with kernel C = F_p(varphi) for some character varphi : G_Q -> F_p^x (equivalently E[p] is reducible), and assume r_an(E) is in {0,1}. Then ord_p(L^*(E/Q,1)/(Omega_E Reg_{E/Q})) = ord_p(Tam(E/Q) #Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity]/(#E(Q)_tors)^2), where L^* is the leading Taylor coefficient at s = 1. In particular NONTRIVIAL p-TORSION IN THE MORDELL-WEIL GROUP IS ALLOWED, and the condition varphi restricted to G_p not equal to 1, omega of CGS Theorem A is removed.
hypotheses: p > 2 of GOOD reduction; E[p] reducible; analytic rank 0 or 1. No condition on varphi at p
The torsion denominator (#E(Q)_tors)^2 is PRESENT in the statement, unlike the CGS and JSW displays; this is the point of the broader branch

The proof requires an ANTICYCLOTOMIC CONTROL THEOREM ALLOWING TORSION SUBMODULES, which Keller-Yin prove in their Appendix B; the JSW control theorem is not sufficient as stated [Annotated in review: 'not sufficient as stated' is an inference. Keller-Yin say only that the [CGLS22, Thm. 5.3.1] argument 'needs an anticyclotomic control theorem which allows torsion submodules' (p. 42). Sec. 0.5 (p. 6) explains that Appendices A and B were developed to allow a nontrivial torsion group H^0(K, rho_f).]

Keller-Yin note that JSW's anticyclotomic Selmer group is the Greenberg Selmer group for f, which agrees with the unramified Selmer group of CGLS only up to a finite kernel; since ker(res_{M_f}) is finite (their Lemma 1.3.6), the two generate the same characteristic ideals

[Corrected in review.] The sentences 'our imprimitive Selmer groups X^S may have finite Lambda-submodules. In particular, the characteristic ideals are no longer identified with the Fitting ideals. The formal argument can be carried out by replacing the Selmer groups by their free parts' (Sec. 0.2, p. 5) concern the Hida-family proof of the MULTIPLICATIVE-reduction Theorem D (Sec. 5.1 item (e) and Lemma 5.1.2, pp. 43-44). They are not a hypothesis of Theorem C. For the good-reduction case, Keller-Yin note (Sec. 0.2, p. 3) that the Selmer groups 'may not be almost divisible ... they might contain non-trivial finite Lambda-submodules'. That is why the Iwasawa-invariant comparisons (0.1)-(0.2) need new arguments.

Their multiplicative-reduction Theorem D (= Theorem 5.1.3) is a MAIN CONJECTURE only; they state explicitly that it would yield rank 0 and rank 1 BSD formulae at multiplicative primes only PROVIDED the results of [CGS23] are extended to higher weight modular forms

[Added in review, OPEN QUESTION (not resolved from the pages read). The Sec. 4.2 proof (pp. 42-43) displays only the rank-one deduction, in which the twist-side rank-zero defect for E^K vanishes 'by [CGLS22, Theorem 5.1.4], a result of Greenberg-Vatsal'. REVIEWER COMPUTATION: chi_K is odd, and chi_K|G_p = 1 because p splits in K. So E^K has kernel character phi.chi_K with (phi.chi_K)|G_p = phi|G_p and the opposite parity. Then neither character of E^K satisfies (GV) as stated in CGS (p. 2: 'unramified at p and odd, or ramified at p and even'), and CGS Theorem A is unavailable because phi|G_p is 1 or omega. The pages read show neither which rank-zero theorem covers E^K in these cases, nor how the rank-zero case of Theorem 4.2.1 is proved when phi|G_p is 1 or omega (for example the listed 11a3 at p = 5, where phi = 1). Keller-Yin's p. 2 also states the Greenberg-Vatsal parity with ramified and unramified reversed, relative to their own p. 42 and to CGS p. 2.]

nodes.title: The Eisenstein-prime main conjectures that the two BSD branches consume
nodes.statement: CGS THEOREM A. Let E/Q be an elliptic curve and p > 2 a prime of GOOD reduction. Suppose p is Eisenstein (E admits a rational p-isogeny phi : E -> E' with G_Q acting on ker(phi) through varphi : G_Q -> F_p^x) with varphi restricted to G_p not equal to 1 or omega. Then X_ord(E/Q_infinity) is Lambda_Q-torsion with ch(X_ord(E/Q_infinity)) = (L^MSD_p(E/Q)), i.e. Mazur's main conjecture holds. KELLER-YIN supply two further inputs: their Theorem 3.0.8 (IMC2), which replaces [CGLS22, Thm. 4.2.2] and removes the condition varphi restricted to G_p not equal to 1, omega; and an ANTICYCLOTOMIC CONTROL THEOREM ALLOWING TORSION SUBMODULES (their Appendix B), without which the [CGLS22, Thm. 5.3.1] argument does not run. Their Theorem D (= Theorem 5.1.3) is a further main conjecture, for weight-two newforms at an odd Eisenstein prime p exactly dividing N of multiplicative reduction, asserting Char(X_f) Lambda_nr = (L_f). [Annotated in review: Keller-Yin's Theorem 3.0.8 (IMC2) = Theorem A (p. 4) takes a newform f in S_k(Gamma_0(N)) with k = 2r and r ODD, p > 2 an ORDINARY Eisenstein prime not dividing N, and K as in Sec. 0.1: all primes dividing N split, D_K odd and != -3, p = v vbar split (p. 2). It concludes that X_f is Lambda-torsion and Char(X_f) Lambda^nr = (L_f). Their Theorem D also assumes K as in Sec. 0.1.]
hypotheses: CGS Theorem A: p > 2 of GOOD reduction, p Eisenstein, and the LOCAL hypothesis varphi restricted to G_p not equal to 1, omega

Before CGS, the statement was known only under Greenberg-Vatsal's hypothesis (GV): varphi either unramified at p and odd, or ramified at p and even. Without (GV) the mu-invariant can be nonzero, by Greenberg's lower bound

[Corrected in review.] The STATEMENT of Keller-Yin's Theorem 3.0.8 (IMC2) was within the pages read, as Theorem A (Sec. 0.2, p. 4), and is recorded in the statement above. Its proof (Sec. 3) and the Appendix B control theorem were NOT read; they are recorded here as named inputs with their stated role.

[Corrected in review.] The 'characteristic ideals are no longer Fitting ideals ... free parts' remark (Sec. 0.2, p. 5) belongs to the Hida-family proof of the multiplicative-reduction Theorem D (Sec. 5.1(e), Lemma 5.1.2, pp. 43-44). For the good-reduction main conjectures, Keller-Yin note that the Selmer groups may contain non-trivial finite Lambda-submodules (Sec. 0.2, p. 3), which is why the comparisons (0.1)-(0.2) need new arguments.

Keller-Yin's Theorem D is a MAIN CONJECTURE at multiplicative primes; they state explicitly that it yields rank 0 and rank 1 BSD formulae there only PROVIDED the results of [CGS23] are extended to higher weight modular forms. It is therefore NOT a BSD input at bad Eisenstein primes as it stands
proofSteps: CGS prove Theorem A by two innovations named in their abstract: a Kolyvagin system argument for the Selmer group of E twisted by anticyclotomic Hecke characters arbitrarily close to the trivial character, and a congruence argument exploiting Beilinson-Flach classes and their explicit reciprocity laws. Their Sections 2-9 were NOT read.

The route is Theorem C (an anticyclotomic statement over K_infinity) reformulated in terms of p-adic L-functions and then transferred to the cyclotomic setting; Theorem C's statement was located but not read in full. [Updated in review: CGS Theorem C (p. 3) says that if p does not divide 2N, p is Eisenstein, K satisfies (Heeg), (disc) and (spl), and phi|G_p != 1, omega, then Perrin-Riou's Conjecture B holds. review.notes: All 10 nodes and 7 draft links were checked against the library copies of JSW (arXiv v1), BFH (300 dpi renders of printed pp. 543-544), CGS (arXiv v2), Keller-Yin (arXiv v2), Castella's erratum (all 5 pages) and Zhang's survey. In addition the reviewer read BSTW pp. 2-4 (library copy, hash matches) and fetched the arXiv abstract pages of 1411.6352 and 1412.1767 into scratch; provenance is in the sources list. The library and catalogue claims were checked: Gross-Zagier yields 224 characters of text and Gross-Kolyvagin 12; CGLS and BSTW hashes match; CLW, CH18, LV19, KO20, Hsieh 2014, EW16 and Kato 2004 are present; Skinner-Zhang, FH95, GV00, Tian and Ribet-Takahashi are absent. The atlas stage texts BSD.0-BSD.9 were read. MAIN CORRECTIONS. (1) JSW rank one: the draft required N^- > 1, quoting the introduction, but the proof uses N^- = 1 when N is prime (pp. 45, 47). Theorems 6.1.4, 6.1.5 and 6.1.6 were conflated: 6.1.4 is two-variable in Lambda_{K,R}[1/p], 6.1.5 is the anticyclotomic statement in Lambda_R[1/p], and 6.1.6 upgrades it to Lambda_R and drops the N D_K condition on Sigma. The CM remark omitted the p-adic height nonvanishing. The description of C^Sigma(W) was imprecise. (2) PROVENANCE: the supersingular case of JSW Theorems 1.2.1 and 7.2.1(iii) rests on [Wan14a] and [Wan14b], both withdrawn on arXiv. BSTW's replacement has a narrower twist range. (3) JSW choose K' and K'' by Friedberg-Hoffstein [FH95, Thm. B] with inert or ramified conditions, which the splitting-only BFH theorem cannot supply. The same holds for CGS's examples and Castella's Theorem 1.1 (a ramified q is forced). (4) Keller-Yin: the Fitting-ideal/free-part remark belongs to the multiplicative Theorem D (Hida argument), not to Theorem C. Theorems C and D are on p. 5, not p. 3. The statement of Theorem 3.0.8 (IMC2) was read (p. 4), contrary to the draft. (5) BSD.5: (7.3.a) as used needs good reduction at p, and the period relation (7.3.e) and its hypotheses were added. papers/ADD_RT97.pdf is Rohrlich-Tunnell, not Ribet-Takahashi. papers/R02_KI_Wan2015.pdf and R02_KI_WanNonordinary.pdf are not JSW's Wan citations. (6) Locators: CGS Theorem A and Greenberg's bound are on p. 2; Zhang's Theorem 1.5 is in Sec. 1.4 on p. 7; JSW's uses of Theorem 7.2.1 are on pp. 47-48.
